meta.title: Aion 2 Macro Sheet
meta.notice: Global (NA/EU) early access opens Sep 30, 2026, with full free-to-play on Oct 5. The Global client can lag the Korea/Taiwan patches this sheet is built on. For example, the Global database still lists Noble Armor and Guardian Blessing at 5 min. If a Global skill doesn't behave as described, check the Global patch notes.
meta.note: Stacks are listed row 0 first (row 0 fires first and sits directly above the key in game). null = empty row. A trailing '?' on a skill name marks an icon-matched row that the source didn't name.

changelog.text: Stigmas page: new Global Season 1 view (4 slots, max level 20) with how high to level each stigma and why, plus the skill specializations (3 of 5) to pick for every class.
Added a Stigmas page (top of the page): 6-slot builds, level-up order with shard costs, milestones, variants (incl. Gladiator battle tank and Chanter battle healer) and tier lists for all 8 classes.

New 'Full rotation' tab for all 8 classes: longer macros with buffs, each with its source and the DPS trade-off. Held/mashed key stacks are now drawn on cards. Gladiator corrected (Rage Burst and Lifestealing Blade sit under Overhead Slam). Level-25 augments corrected for 8 stigmas changed after July. KR/TW cooldowns for Warding Strike, Spinning Strike and Impactful Crush. Zikel's Blessing and Lunge Stance icons fixed (swapped in the database). Templar switched to the optimizer's Sep 5 guide, pinned as current after Sep 16 (Shield Smite in the Judgment line, Annihilate as line 2, Flash Rampage above Punishment).
Added the missing Stigma level-25 specialty to the hover card of all 37 stigma skills on the sheet (read from KR in-game tooltips, Inven, Jul 1 2026).

Hover any skill for its description, range and specialty unlocks. "Other versions" are now drawn as full macro stacks. Vicious Strike and Pummel now use the player-skill database entries (no cooldown; Pummel costs 120 MP). Taiwan Ranger stacks decoded.

Real skill icons and cooldowns added. Stacks now drawn bottom-up like the game. Review fixes: Ranger skill-queue note, Assassin Storm Rampage key, Templar Annihilate/Punishment keys, TW Sorcerer and Chanter rows re-read, Noble Armor and Guardian Blessing cooldowns set to the post-patch 2 min.
Late-game stacks from Korean guides dated Sep 5 to Sep 24. Improved early-game builds. Chaining guide.

late.src: Inven 9/18 (post-patch), matches TW 5/27 and the video
late.queue: Not stated in the source, so test both
late.why: One slot does the work. Insignia Explosion fires first, Heart Gore fires whenever a crit unlocks it, and Savage Roar fills the gaps. The source also holds its Storm Rampage line (the B key in its screenshot) at the same time, so the Storm Rampage cancel fires on its own during stagger windows.
late.tip: Keep Ambush out of every macro line. The source tested it and hits dropped. Press it by hand, ideally on a turbo key. Ambush specs: take #1 and #4, not #5.
late.patch: Sep 16: longer cancel delay on Savage Roar, Savage Smash and Heart Gore. +10% PvE on Insignia Explosion and the slice skills.

alts.s: Both entries at 10 ms.
Both use the same single macro slot: Insignia Explosion → Heart Gore → Savage Roar. One holds left click (Quick Slice) + the macro; the other also mashes Storm Rampage and Ambush on their own keys.

early.why: This is the late-game order, so you never have to relearn it. Insignia Explosion detonates up to 5 Insignia stacks. Heart Gore only lights up after a crit, so the macro skips it until then. Savage Roar is the filler that builds stacks. Ambush from behind adds 2 stacks, so press it yourself.
early.tip: While leveling, hold Quick Slice with the macro because it restores MP. Its +20% MP-restored specialty fixes early mana shortages.

alts.s: Same firing order as the improved build. The empty row 2 just wastes a spot you can use later.

full.src: Built from the Inven 9/18 layout's buff keys (the macro line is the tested one)
full.why: Line 1 is the tested damage line. Line 2 fires your burst skills in the order that feeds it: Illusive Clone removes Heart Gore's cooldown for 10 s, Savage Fang engraves 5 Insignias so the next Insignia Explosion hits at full stacks, then Triniel's Dagger (+10% back damage at 25) and Assault Ambush.
full.loss: Heart Gore is checked every other loop instead of every loop, and burst buffs also fire on trash or during mechanics. Expect a few percent lower DPS than the 1-line setup (for scale, a second line cost Gladiator 5–6% of its main hits).
full.tip: Keep Ambush and Storm Slice out of the macro and press them yourself; the source found Ambush in any line lowers hits.

late.queue: Asked on Inven 9/8 with no consensus, so test both
late.why: This order gave the highest, smoothest damage in testing. Hold Lightning Strike Scattershot with the macro and its cancel fires in stagger windows, which also lowers cooldowns.
late.tip: Bolt stays manual so a charge never delays a heal. Use Debilitating Mark only when the party is hurting, because casting it on cooldown loses damage. Judgment Thunder is for trash. Aim for 32.6% cooldown reduction. Level Condemnation, Earth's Retribution, Bolt and Divine Aura to 20. Take Earth's Grace before Empyrean Lord's Grace.
late.patch: Cleric attack speed caps at 94.4% while other classes reach about 121.6%. That's why two macro lines cost Cleric almost nothing.

alts.s: Three entries with delays of 40, 20 and 20 ms. Hold Earth's Retribution with the macro key. The Korean 9/24 guide found Debilitating Mark on cooldown loses damage, so this setup is superseded.
A separate player: taking Debilitating Mark out of the Condemnation macro raised DPS, which matches the 9/24 guide.

early.why: Use the tested late-game stack from the start. Rows you haven't learned yet are skipped. Condemnation sits above Chain of Torment because it only hits chained targets. When the chain is missing, Condemnation is skipped and Chain of Torment fires, so the order fixes itself.
early.tip: For leveling trash packs, also hold Judgment Thunder on its own key. The Korean guide uses it only for trash, and a key you hold covers that without costing the macro a line.

alts.s: Korean testing (9/24) found Debilitating Mark on cooldown loses damage, so it moved to manual, and Judgment Thunder moved out for trash-only use.

full.src: Inven 9/24 two-line option (rows 1–2 of each line are from the guide)
full.why: The 9/24 guide splits Condemnation → Chain of Torment and Earth Punishment → Divine Aura into two lines and leaves the empty rows for 'skills you want automatic'. Noble Aura (a 5-minute summon) and Prayer of Amplification (party damage buff, stronger since Aug 26) fill them, so your whole damage kit plus two buffs run from one key.
full.loss: Cleric loses almost nothing from a second line because its attack speed caps at 94.4%, so this is the cheapest full rotation of any class. Prayer of Amplification is best saved for burst windows, so it's the part you give up by automating.
full.tip: Keep Bolt manual so a charge never delays a heal, and keep heals on their own keys.

late.queue: Debated on Inven 9/21, so test both
late.why: Only one macro line: Sorcerer loses the most damage of any class from a second line. The held Hellfire key reproduces the manual timing. Delayed Explosion goes first, Hellfire follows fully charged, then Winter's Shackles, and Flame Scattershot sits at the top so its stagger cancel fires on its own. That key's stack is from the Aug 27 top-DPS post; the Sep 22 guide describes the same key.
late.tip: Opener: Element Enhancement → Delayed Explosion → full-charge Hellfire → drop Fire Wall and Cold Storm → hold. Keep the ground AoEs in one slot and mash it when the boss stands still. Level Hellfire, Blaze, Firestorm and Wish of Concentration to 20, then Bittercold Wind. Sorcerer needs only one passive, and the guide says to push it toward level 36.
late.patch: Sep 16: Fire Mark now procs 100%, and Blaze no longer consumes it.

alts.s: Same three-key setup (skill macro, basic attack, Hellfire key). Viewers point out the author keeps Winter's Shackles on its own key instead of in the Hellfire line, and a viewer reported +250k DPS and +70 hits/min after copying the mouse-macro setup.

alts.t: TW Bahamut 5/27 (pre-patch, rows read from icons)
alts.s: Four entries, all 10 ms. Flame Arrow is also the basic attack.

early.why: One line, in the order the 9/22 guide found best. The video used a second entry just for Ice Chain. Sorcerer loses more from a second line than any other class, so that entry cost hits on your main damage.
early.tip: Press Winter's Shackles yourself when a pack reaches you, instead of letting the macro spend it on one mob. Ice Chain (no cooldown) is your mana tool, so press it when MP runs low. Full-charge Hellfire by hand.

alts.s: The second entry holds only Ice Chain. Sorcerer loses the most hits from extra lines.

full.src: Inven 8/27 top-DPS post (image-verified: both lines exactly as shown)
full.why: The author's own setup: line 2 automates Element Enhancement and both ground AoEs. Since a patch shortened their animations, they say it's fine to keep the Element Enhancement line in the macro rather than pressing it.
full.loss: Sorcerer is the class that loses the most per extra line. The AoE line can also fire before the Delayed Explosion and Winter's Shackles buffs are up (a 9/20 player saw exactly this), and ground AoEs are wasted when the boss moves.
full.tip: Opener: Element Enhancement → Delayed Explosion → full-charge Hellfire → Fire Wall → Cold Storm → macro on. The author notes the Hellfire key sometimes gets stuck, so tap it again if it stops.

late.src: Inven 9/5 optimizer guide, pinned as current after 9/16 (image-verified)
late.queue: Not stated; the 9/16 and 9/17 players disagree (OFF / ON), so test both
late.why: Pummel sits in the same line as Judgment. That's what makes your held Vicious Strike cancel straight into Judgment (the 'Vicious–Judgment' cancel), which the guide's author pinned as the one to use after the Sep 16 patch killed the Pummel–Judgment cancel. Shield Smite and Warding Strike are shield attacks, so they re-open Judgment (Aug 26 rework). Annihilate gets its own macro line. Flash Rampage sits above Punishment on the charge key so its stagger cancel fires on its own.
late.tip: Opener: press Noble Armor, Battlefield Banner and Empyrean Lord's Punishment, full-charge Punishment for the Executor buff, then rush in. Top-end trick: Doom Shield resets Annihilate, so Annihilate → Doom Shield → Annihilate. Pummel and Judgment go to 20. Use Shield of Protection every ~20 s or on boss crowd-control mechanics.
late.patch: Sep 16: longer cancel delay on Pummel, Punishing Strike and Judgment. Warding Strike, Annihilate and Punishment +10% PvE, Shield Smite +20%. Noble Armor 5 min → 2 min. Taunt threat now scales with damage.

alts.s: Doom Shield instead of Shield Smite in row 2, skill queue OFF, and Annihilate and Punishment on their own mouse-macro keys.

Doom Shield and Shield Smite both in the line, no Pummel, skill queue ON; a second key (Annihilate → Noble Armor → Battlefield Banner → Empyrean Lord's Punishment) is mashed. See the Full rotation tab.
Annihilate is kept on its own key.

early.why: The same line the late-game guide uses, and every skill in it is learned early (Doom Shield is a level-22 stigma, so it stays manual). With one line, Judgment is checked every loop. Shield Smite and Warding Strike are shield attacks, so they keep re-opening Judgment, and Pummel in the same line makes your held Vicious Strike cancel into it.
early.tip: Hold Vicious Strike (left click) with the macro, and take its +20% MP-restored specialty for leveling. When you get Doom Shield, press it to open fights (it rushes 20 m and shields you).

alts.t: Video version (also matches your in-game bar)
alts.s: Judgment sits in row 2 here, so it fires late in its short window.

full.why: Line 1 is the Vicious Strike → Judgment damage line; Shield Smite and Doom Shield keep Judgment lit (Judgment now opens after any shield attack). Line 2 adds Annihilate plus your buffs: Noble Armor (2 min since Sep 16), Battlefield Banner and Empyrean Lord's Punishment. The author says line 2 works in the macro, but mashing it on its own key did slightly better.
full.loss: Another Templar (Aug 28) notes that automating Banner and Empyrean Lord's Punishment costs speed and can overlap a Chanter's Power of the Storm. Press them yourself in groups if you want the top number.
full.tip: Skill queue ON for this setup. Charge Punishment yourself (or bind it to a mouse key).

late.queue: Not stated in the source, so test both
late.why: "Dark–Spin–Impact–Incandescent" was the most stable order. Holding Gust Rampage adds its stagger cancel, which lowers its cooldown and keeps the damage going.
late.tip: Stack Guardian Blessing on top of Power of the Storm so it never gets forgotten. That frees keys for Undefeated Mantra and Sprint Mantra, which are toggle skills that must never go in a macro, because a second press switches them off. Marchutan's Wrath is no longer required, so swap in a utility stigma or Fracturing Blow. Dark Crush and Onslaught go to 20, and Spinning Strike and Recuperation are close behind. Passives: Wind's Promise, Impact Hit, Attack Preparation.
late.patch: Sep 16: Guardian Blessing 5 min → 2 min. Earlier bugs where Marchutan's Wrath or Spinning Strike got eaten are fixed.

alts.s: The three Dark Crush openers stop overlapping, which gave +3–5 Dark Crush/min and ~+100–150k in Expedition. That's one player's full-auto test, not a top-end setup.

alts.t: Viewer test on the Sep 2 Chanter guide video (single source)
alts.s: A commenter on the 43k-view Sep 2 guide by 하구 tested moving Spinning Strike to its own key and pressing it on cooldown: +1.5–2% DPS. It's the same idea as the Impactful Crush split: stop the Dark Crush openers from overlapping.
Three entries, all 10 ms. Hold basic attack with the macro.
A six-step sequence, drawn here as six entries. Korean testing shows every extra line cuts damage, so treat it as a skill-priority list rather than a macro to copy. Keep Charged Rushing Smash out.

early.why: The video used two entries (Spinning Strike alone, then the Dark Crush stack). One line with Dark Crush in row 0 does the same job with half the loop turns. Spinning Strike (20 m, hits 4, +15% crit damage) and Impactful Crush open Dark Crush windows, and Dark Crush in row 0 catches every one.
early.tip: Add Gust Rampage as a third held key once you have it. If Impactful Crush isn't learned yet, put Marchutan's Wrath in that row. Keep Rushing Smash manual because it's a charge skill.

alts.s: Two entries, where the improved build needs one.

full.src: Inven 9/3 full-auto test (lines 1–2 image-verified) + 9/17 buff stack
full.why: Lines 1–2 are the '100% in-game macro' setup a 900k Chanter built so nothing needs pressing: splitting Impactful Crush out stops the three Dark Crush openers from overlapping (+3–5 Dark Crush/min). Line 3 adds the 9/17 guide's buff stack so Power of the Storm and Guardian Blessing run themselves.
full.loss: Three lines means each slot is checked a third of the time. Power of the Storm is a party burst buff, so automating it can waste it outside burst windows, and in the Abyss 'Battlefield Might' replaces it during boss fights.
full.tip: Never macro Undefeated or Sprint Mantra: they're toggles, and a second press switches them off.

late.queue: Not stated in the source, so test both
late.why: Sword Aura Rampage sits directly under Rending Blow so its stagger cancel fires cleanly. Hold basic attack and the macro while mashing Overhead Slam. That is the Overhead Slam→Rending Blow cancel (内絕 / 내절), which came back on Aug 26.
late.tip: Opener: buffs → Ruinous Blow (Prepare for Battle) → start weaving. Rage Burst and Lifestealing Blade sit under Overhead Slam on the mashed key, so they fire the moment they're ready. Press Lunge Stance, Zikel's Blessing and Wave Armor yourself so they aren't wasted during mechanics or on trash (both the top-end and comfort layouts in the 9/5 guide do this). Aerial Snare under Overhead Slam adds DPS. Aim for ~97–102 Upward Strike hits per minute. Rending Blow and Overhead Slam go to 20. Passives: Experienced Counterstrike and Murderous Burst first.
late.patch: Sep 16: Leaping Slam and Ruinous Blow can't be used while bound. Sep 23: Fracturing Rush now follows your key direction.

alts.s: Two single-skill entries. Buffs sit stacked on a separate key and are pressed by hand.

early.why: This uses the late-game structure right away. Until Sword Aura Rampage is learned, row 0 is skipped and the slot is just Rending Blow. Overhead Slam goes on its own key that you hold or tap alongside. Korean testing showed that putting it in the macro as a second line costs hits.
early.tip: Easy option from the 9/5 guide: on the Overhead Slam key, put Rage Burst and Lifestealing Blade in rows 0–1 with Overhead Slam above them, so your buffs fire the moment they're ready. Open with Ruinous Blow for Prepare for Battle (+20% PvE damage).

alts.s: It works, but Overhead Slam can't be mashed and Rage Burst gets spent on trash.

full.why: The guide's own comfort setup: every stigma fires by itself. Rage Burst and Lifestealing Blade lead the macro line, and the buffs sit under Overhead Slam on the mashed key, which the guide says makes them turn on faster than a second macro line would.
full.loss: The guide recommends pressing stigmas yourself for the top number, because automated buffs get wasted during mechanics and on trash. Adding the buffs as a second macro line instead costs even more (a second line cost 5–6% of Overhead Slam hits in an Aug 12 test).
full.tip: Start fights with Ruinous Blow for Prepare for Battle, then hold.

late.why: The four-spirit setup tested highest. The spirit line goes into the macro, and only the Fusion slot is mashed separately. Water → Earth first keeps skills from getting eaten and keeps the Fire Spirit up.
late.tip: Opener: buffs → Earth Tremor at 4–5 stacks and Element Unification full → summon the Ancient Spirit → 3–4 s later, full-charge Destructive Attack. For comfort, put Rapid Scattershot on the Destructive Attack key; for top numbers, keep it separate. Its cancel fires on its own during stagger. Fight from about 3 m. Keep Cold Shock's 5-stack attack buff running. Passives: Spirit Strike, Element Unification, Mental Focus.
late.patch: Sep 10: Destructive Attack's spirit follow-up now fires instantly (Jointstrike overwrite bug fixed).

alts.s: A different tested approach: skill queue OFF so the macro skills always win, Elemental Fusion and the spirits in the in-game macro, Curse / Dimensional Control / Combustion mashed by mouse software, and Corrode kept out (it fires on trash and scrambles cooldowns). Opener: hold macro → Corrode → wait for party buffs (Power of the Storm, Fury, Earth Punishment) → Flame Blessing → Spirit's Benediction → Ancient Spirit → Destructive Attack → Corrode.
Spirits are stacked on key 1 and pressed by hand.

early.why: Two lines are justified for this class because the spirits run on their own 15 s timers. The three-spirit order Water → Earth → Fire had the fewest eaten casts. When you get the fourth spirit, add Wind in row 2 ahead of Fire. Each spirit skill gives an Element that Elemental Fusion spends. Fusion moves to its own key and gets tapped, which tested higher than keeping it in the macro.
early.tip: Water Spirit hits return 20 MP, so always keep it in row 0. Keep Cold Shock (left click) held too, because its 5-stack attack buff is your core self-buff.

alts.s: This mixes debuffs into the spirit line and leaves Fusion in the loop.

full.src: Inven 9/16 lines + the 9/06 player's buff stack
full.why: Everything except the timing-sensitive burst runs from one key: debuffs, all four spirits, Fusion and your two self-buffs. Ancient Spirit and Destructive Attack stay manual because the guide times them (Ancient Spirit after Earth Tremor 4–5 stacks, Destructive Attack 3–4 s later).
full.loss: Elemental Fusion in the macro tested lower than mashing it on its own key (9/16), and four lines spread the loop thin. Another tested guide (8/13) keeps Corrode out because it fires on trash and scrambles cooldowns.
full.tip: Fight from about 3 m. If Fusion stacks feel slow, pull line 3 back out and tap Fusion yourself; that recovers most of the loss.

late.queue: OFF in both 9/6 setups; a 9/3 tester prefers ON (buffs press instantly) and saw little DPS difference.
late.why: Tempest Shot sits at the top of a different line from the short-cooldown skills. That gives the "Tempest Shot cancel": more Tempest Shot hits and ~3% more damage. Arrow Scattershot goes directly under it, so the stagger cancel lands 12–30 hits.
late.tip: Level Deadshot, Gale Arrow and Snare Shot to 20. Snare Shot needs the move-cast spec plus Shackling Arrow (+2–3%). Cast Marking Shot standing still, and refresh it with ~2 s left. Passives: Focused Eye and Hunter's Resolve.
late.patch: Sep 16: every Ranger attack has an element. Drill Dart, Griffon and Explosive Arrow are Fire.

alts.s: Four entries, all 10 ms. Tempest Shot sits at the top of the Gale Arrow line here.

early.why: The video put Tempest Shot on the Drill Dart line. Ranger testing says Tempest Shot must never sit under Drill Dart. At the top of the Griffon line it gets the Tempest Shot cancel instead. Two lines is the Ranger maximum, and any row you haven't learned is skipped.
early.tip: Griffon Arrow hits 4 targets and burns them for 10 s, which makes it great for leveling pulls. Press buffs yourself, because buffs in the macro drop Snipe hits.

alts.s: Tempest Shot sits on the Drill Dart line. Ranger testing says it must not sit under Drill Dart.

full.why: Lines 1–2 are the tested Tempest Shot cancel setup. Line 3 is the buff line an Aug 30 Ranger runs in their one-click setup (Vaizel's Authority → Supporting Fire → Bow of Blessing). They measured no real DPS difference against the tuned 28-Deadshot setup on the dummy.
full.loss: A Sep 3 Ranger warns that buffs in the macro can drop Snipe below 16–18 hits/min. Check Snipe on the dummy, and if it drops, press the buffs yourself.
full.tip: Cast Marking Shot yourself while standing still, refreshing it with ~2 s left.
